question: Tell me about a decision you wrote down so that people who were not in the room could act on it.

raiseTranscript.text: After a code review on a new feature flag, I wrote a short decision log in the wiki explaining why we chose the default value and rollout criteria so the on-call team could handle incidents without me.
The trade-off on performance vs safety, the rollback steps, and who to ping if it went wrong. Two engineers used it the next week.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a decision you wrote down so that people who were not in the room could act on it.
Role: junior dev on feature flag rollout
Situation: post-review, wrote wiki entry with defaults, trade-offs, rollback
Action: included performance/safety reasoning and escalation path
Outcome: on-call used it twice without needing clarification
Quote: 'Two engineers used it the next week.'
Follow-up: What did you include exactly? -> detailed the trade-off and steps
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Transparency for the question. Junior candidate documented a feature-flag default decision in the wiki with trade-offs, rollback steps, and escalation so on-call engineers could act independently. Quote: 'Two engineers used it the next week.' This shows ownership of making individual work reusable by others. The detail level matches junior scope while demonstrating coachability through written artifacts rather than verbal handoff. Biggest strength is the concrete, low-scope artifact that reduced follow-up questions.

lowerTranscript.text: I told the team in standup what we decided on the flag default.

They could ask me or check the PR comments.

junior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar on Transparency for the question. Junior candidate shared the flag default only verbally in standup and pointed to PR comments for anyone absent. Biggest gap is absence of any artifact that allows independent action.

raiseTranscript.text: After a cross-team API change, I wrote a one-pager on the deprecation timeline and migration steps, posted it to the shared doc site, and linked it from the service catalog so other teams could plan without attending our syncs.
Two teams adjusted their roadmaps early; one asked for an extension which we granted based on the documented criteria.

Action: posted to doc site and service catalog
Outcome: two teams adjusted roadmaps; one extension request handled via criteria
Quote: 'Two teams adjusted their roadmaps early.'

senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Transparency for the question. Senior candidate produced a one-pager on API deprecation timeline and migration steps, published to the service catalog so absent teams could act. Quote: 'Two teams adjusted their roadmaps early.' Shows influence across teams through written artifacts. The outcome demonstrates reduced coordination overhead. Biggest strength is the measurable cross-team impact from a documented decision rather than meetings.

lowerTranscript.text: I sent an email to the affected teams about the API change timeline.
Did teams outside the original group use it to plan?
A couple replied with questions, so I answered in the thread.

senior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar on Transparency for the question. Senior candidate sent a single email on API timeline and handled questions in the thread. This shows cross-team intent but lacks the durable artifact needed for influence without authority. Biggest gap is reliance on synchronous or threaded follow-up instead of a reusable decision document.

raiseTranscript.text: After deciding to sunset a product line, I wrote a memo covering the business rationale, customer migration plan, and 18-month timeline, then posted it to the company wiki and presented the link at the all-hands so every org could align their plans.
How did it affect long-term decisions?
Three divisions reallocated headcount based on the published criteria; we avoided two redundant investment proposals.
